body: One bit of the signature. The first byte and the last are flipped separately: they fail for different reasons and through different code. A flip anywhere makes the recovered block effectively random, so what is actually being tested is that SOME check fires rather than which one.

author: reek
body: A signature of the wrong width, refused before any arithmetic.

author: reek
body: THE TWO CHECKS ON THE RECOVERED BLOCK. Neither is reachable by altering a signature from outside: any change to the bytes makes the recovered block effectively random and it fails at the digest comparison instead, so with both checks deleted every other line in this test is unchanged. That was measured, not assumed.

author: reek
body: The control is the load-bearing line. Without it, two rejections prove only that hand-built signatures do not verify, which would be true of anything. With it, the construction is known good and each forgery differs from it in exactly one place.
